`listDirectory`/`existsDirectory` branch by path shape in a fixed, load-bearing order — shadow, atomic-shard-dir, table-uuid, part-file, table-subdir, generic mirrored LIST — because `store/<u3>` and non-Atomic `data/<db>` would otherwise collide, so `isAtomicShardDir` must be consulted before `parseTableUuid`.

Every CAS key family is rooted at `POOL = pool_prefix`: blob body `POOL/blobs/<algo>/<S>/<hex>` (self-describing, `<S>`=first 2 hex chars); blob meta `POOL/blobs/<algo>/<S>/<hex>.meta`; part manifest `POOL/cas/manifests/<ns>/<epoch-hex>-<seq-hex>/<NNNNNN>.proto`; ref log txn `POOL/cas/refs/<ns>/_log/<render>`; ref snapshot `POOL/cas/refs/<ns>/_snap/<render>.proto`; ref cleanup marker `POOL/cas/refs/<ns>/_cleanup/<render>`; verbatim namespace file `POOL/roots/<ns>/_files/<name>`; plain mountpoint object `POOL/roots/<key>`; pool meta `POOL/_pool_meta`; GC state/heartbeat `POOL/gc/state`, `POOL/gc/hb`; GC generation artifacts `POOL/gc/gen/<gen>/attempt/<a>/...`; server-root control `POOL/gc/server-roots/<srid>/{owner,epoch,mount}`; opt-in staging `POOL/staging/<mount_id>/...` (a distinct top-level sibling GC never LISTs).

`CasPoolMeta` (`_pool_meta`) is a pure protobuf `PoolMetaProto` holding `pool_id`, `root_shards`, `blob_header_len`, `min_reader_generation`, and a sorted append-only `algos_used[]`; invariants are `root_shards >= 1` and `blob_header_len` 8-aligned in `[96, 16384]`; admitting a new hash algorithm raises `min_reader_generation` to `G_BUILD` in the same CAS.
Phase 2 pluggable-hash `sha256` blobs are stored under the key shape `blobs/sha256/<shard>/<64-hex>`, distinct from the default 128-bit hash's `blobs/<aa>/<H>` layout.
S3-native staging is opt-in and streams to staging before a capability-probed conditional server-side-copy promote, with fail-closed fallback to local scratch.

The retired-in-snapshot plan makes each per-shard source-edge run carry condemned state at the existing zero-sentinel key, adds a per-shard `CondemnedSummary` to the fold seal, and removes `RetiredSet`, `CART`, `retiredKey`, and `GcState::retired_refs`.
`GcState::retired_refs` is removed and its protobuf field number is reserved; `GcState` retains round, fence, shard, snapshot, manifest-sweep, and lease fields without retired-object references.
A CAS pool may contain blobs under several hash algorithms without migration or rehashing; old blobs retain their original algorithm and new writes use the configured algorithm.
Settlement uses source-edge key schema 3 with key bytes `algo(u8) ++ digest[blobHashLenFor(algo)] ++ source_id(16 BE)`, producing 33-byte keys for 16-byte algorithms and 49-byte keys for SHA-256.
S3-native staging is opt-in per disk and off by default; large blobs stream to `POOL/staging/<mount_id>/<rnd>.tmp`, then promote to the content key by write-once conditional server-side copy.
`Layout::blobKey`, `Layout::blobMetaKey`, and `Layout::parseBlobKey` are defined in a dedicated `CasLayout.cpp` because including `CasBlobRef.h` from `CasLayout.h` would create an include cycle.

The pre-release CAS format cleanup removes the scalar `root_shards` from `PoolConfig`/`PoolMeta`, removes its proto field, and reserves proto field number 3 and name `root_shards`; the live `FoldResult::root_shards` vector is unrelated and must remain.

The `_precommits` namespace model and `isPrecommitNamespace` are dead because production ref keys use `_log/`, `_snap/`, and `_cleanup/`; their format modeling is removed without compatibility scaffolding.

The pure-visit pagination loops in `CasRefIntake.cpp` and `CasServerRoot.cpp` are candidates for a shared `forEachListedKey` helper, but adding stop-on-true or page-boundary control would require an interface design before migrating `deletePrefixWholesale` and namespace-cleanup passes.

The identity micro-header merge places `RootNamespace`, `Token`, `BlobDigest`, `BlobRef`, `ManifestId`, and `RefTxnId` in `CasTypes.h`, while codec and hex helpers remain in the separate `CasCodecUtil.h` file.
`CasPlainObjects` is stateless over `Backend &` and `const Layout &`, and `CasStore` retains the external API through thin delegates.
On the Atomic layout, `moving` already occupies the parser's part-directory position, so the L1 fix adds a `route()` case rather than changing `findPartDirComponent` for that layout.

The preferred S36/S37 fix is to keep placement-check payloads below `ROUTE_THRESHOLD_BYTES` at every scale by increasing part count rather than per-part bytes; raising `max_data_part_size_bytes` is less preferred because it weakens S37's deliberate 4 MiB routing test.

`_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and transaction-addressed, grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup; moving it to `state/` would require a second hot LIST or a simultaneous recovery-and-cleanup redesign. Additionally, `_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and sequence-addressed, is grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup, and avoids a second hot LIST; the stream/state split is by access pattern, not ownership.

The catalog entry's incarnation is the opaque physical `life_id` shared by the ref layer and namespace files; the logical `RootNamespace` remains in catalog entries and in-memory `NamespaceLifeId` values but is absent from life-owned object keys.
A projection is represented by nested `<proj>.proj/<file>` keys inside the parent part's single `PartManifest`; nested sub-manifests and a separate `projections/` ref namespace were rejected.
Removing the namespace registry requires two independent coordinates: a never-reused per-`(ns,shard)` incarnation for identity and the pool-global GC round as the newborn shard's self-fence.
The namespace registry can be deleted without an ephemeral `pending-newborns` fallback because the newborn self-floor plus per-round LIST fencing preserves `INV_NO_DANGLING`.
The D1 shard-incarnation and registry-removal work deleted `gc/registry`, stamps `ShardIncarnation` in `CasRootShardCodec.h`, and discovers the universe with `LIST`-based `discoverUniverse`.

`openObject` rejects a compressed body under a raw-compression policy, but passes a non-zstd body through verbatim under an `Always` policy as an intentional uncompressed-repair path; in normal operation `Always` objects are read through `.zst`-suffixed keys.
The candidate codec substrate may centralize version checks and named `UInt128` wire helpers, but must not unify or change the three existing on-disk byte orders.

The consistency review recommends using `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION` or `UNKNOWN_FORMAT` for future CAS on-disk versions, keeping `CORRUPTED_DATA` for malformed data and reserving `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for unsupported operations.

The embedded CARN stream in PartManifest should be retained only if PartManifest gains a real streaming reader or shares typed CARN validation; otherwise CAPT should become fully self-contained custom binary or protobuf

RunFile is justified for large sorted streams requiring bounded-memory merge, ranged seek, and replay or adoption of write-once run objects, but is less compelling for small embedded sections materialized whole
Typed CARN helpers should include openManifestEntriesRun, openBlobTargetRun, and openPartManifestCleanupRun and validate RunKind, key_schema, codec, and block-size invariants
Every self-describing CAS object in v2 begins with one universal 8-byte little-endian CasPreamble containing magic, writer_version, and compatibility_version
The shared v2 helpers encodeFramedProto and decodeFramedProto own framing, compression, magic, compatibility, and parse boilerplate; per-object codecs only map fields and validate invariants
v2 drops PartManifest.payload_digest because body_crc32c subsumes its guard role and the field was neither a key nor verified during reads
v3 makes every metadata byte human-readable with head, zstdcat, jq, less, and diff; raw blob payload remains the only non-metadata binary region
On mutable objects, additive JSON fields are designed to be safe-to-lose because an old-build read-modify-write can omit them until the pool floor rises
DataPartStorageContentAddressed addresses only part identity -> manifest entries and files; it does not replace table identity -> durable set of physical parts.

GC uses a hot `cas/refs/` path for listed reference metadata and a cold `cas/manifests/` path for cursor-paged manifest bodies; discovery is `GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/` with cost proportional to reference shards.

`DiskObjectStorageCache::wrapWithCache` must reuse the CAS metadata storage instead of a generic cache-passthrough wrapper because the generic wrapper hides `isContentAddressed` and concrete CAS types used by read and write paths. Additionally, `DiskObjectStorage::wrapWithCache` reuses the CA metadata storage directly instead of wrapping it in the generic `MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage`, because the generic wrapper would hide `isContentAddressed()` and the concrete types the CA read/write paths `dynamic_cast` to, forcing the write path into `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; only the object storage is cached, control-plane traffic bypasses the cache via the CA storage's own raw object-storage pointer.

The current `PartPathParser` behavior favors parsing real detached directories into the table namespace, so an exotic non-Atomic identifier named `detached` can be misparsed and `parseTableUuid` can return `nullopt` for its bare table directory.
The codecs-v3 audit concluded that all 15 live persisted CAS objects have text codecs under `Core/Formats/`, no `.proto` files remain, and both binary codecs were deleted.

With `root_shards=8` and a 96 KiB trim cap, observed shard bodies still reached 588 KB because the tail above the sealed cursor is round-cadence-bound; one key accumulated 8,471 leaked RustFS directories in 30 minutes.
A `ca_stress` Wide part wrote about 26.8 files but generated about 5.8 blob-body writes and one manifest write because small files were inlined into the manifest.
The v2 target reduces the format structure from five families plus one exception to three families plus explicit raw passthrough and reduces version gates to one name pair at one pre-parse position
v3 targets three families plus explicit raw passthrough, zero unversioned objects, one version field gated on line 1, and removal of protobuf and code generation from the subsystem
The multidisk placement policies used by S36 and S37 set `max_data_part_size_bytes` to `4194304` bytes (4 MiB) on their hot volumes.
S37 is commissioned to test multi-disk policies containing local and CA disks, including mixed-disk merges and atomic restart recovery during policy moves.
